sentences.text: Plateosaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur, a group of early herbivores often referred to as prosauropods.
Fully grown individuals ranged from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and weighed between 600 and 4000 kilograms.

This bipedal herbivore featured a long mobile neck, blunt but sharp teeth for crushing plants, powerful hind legs, and short but muscular arms with grasping hands containing large claws on three fingers.
The animal walked on its toes with hind limbs held under its body, utilizing slightly flexed knees and ankles.
The skull was small and narrow, appearing rectangular in side view and almost three times longer than it was tall.
Due to the abundance of fossils found in Swabia, Germany, the species earned the nickname 'Swabian lindworm'.
These dinosaurs commonly lived for at least 12 to 20 years, although their maximum lifespan remains unknown.
The geologically oldest species, P. gracilis, was smaller, reaching a total length of only 4 to 5 meters.
The genus was formally described by Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
The initial discovery of fossils occurred in 1834 at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany.
In 1837, von Meyer described the bones as belonging to a gigantic Saurian with massive and hollow limb bones, allied to Iguanodon and Megalosaurus.
More than 100 skeletons have been discovered, making it one of the best-known dinosaurs.
Plateosaurus was an obligate biped because it lacked the ability to pronate its forelimbs.
The animal likely increased its speed by using higher stride frequencies generated by rapid and powerful limb retraction.
No fossil of Plateosaurus has been found containing gastroliths in the stomach area.
Pathologies on the chevrons of specimen SMNS 13200, a Plateosaurus skeleton, are hypothesized to result from capture myopathy caused by getting trapped in mud.
Martin Sander confirmed Fraas's mud-miring hypothesis, finding that animals above a certain weight sank into mud that liquefied as they struggled to free themselves.
Plateosaurus exhibited a growth pattern similar to sauropods but with variable rates and final sizes, likely due to environmental factors like food availability.
Analysis of rib articulation suggests the animal had a lung air volume of approximately 20 liters for an individual weighing 690 kilograms, or 29 ml/kg of body weight.
As of 2019, only three species of Plateosaurus are universally accepted as valid: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
There is no extended consensus on the taxonomy of Plateosaurus species.
Plateosaurus lived during the Late Triassic epoch, approximately 214 to 204 million years ago.
It is debated whether Plateosaurus was the direct ancestor of sauropods.
Paul Barrett proposed that Plateosaurus was an omnivore that supplemented its herbivorous diet with small prey or carrion.
Until the 1980s, paleontologists debated whether prosauropods like Plateosaurus were carnivorous.
